statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Gibraltar Companies Registry (CSRG) / Companies House Gibraltar (electronic filing portal)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: English is the sole official language; company names must be expressed in Latin (Roman) script and comply with the Companies Act 2014 nomenclature rules. Foreign-language names require a certified English transliteration or translation approved by the Registrar.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection, the applicant may file a written administrative appeal with the Registrar of Companies within 21 days of rejection notice, stating grounds of objection and proposed compliance with statutory naming rules. The Registrar must issue a reasoned determination within 30 days. If the appeal is denied, the applicant may challenge the decision via judicial review in the Supreme Court of Gibraltar. A rejected name may be resubmitted after a 30-day cooling-off period with amended wording.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Virtual office is acceptable for this low-risk digital stock photography and generative visual assets business, provided a licensed corporate service provider maintains a registered office address in Gibraltar, statutory registers are stored in Gibraltar or accessible electronically, and the registered office can accept service of process and statutory correspondence.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: 5-10% annual probability for a low-risk commercial stock media platform; unannounced inspections are conducted only upon suspicion of non-compliance or sanctioned activity, with 48-hour advance notice for ordinary verification unless an inspection warrant is obtained.

incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Incorporation of a Company (Form INC-G) together with Memorandum and Articles of Association
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital requirement; share capital may be denominated in any currency; no escrow account rule applies to a standard private limited company.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED that the allotment and issue of one subscription share of no par value to the initial subscriber be, and the same is hereby, approved and recorded in the register of members. FURTHER RESOLVED that the registered office of the Company be established at [address], Gibraltar, and the Company Secretary be instructed to file the notice of registered office with the Gibraltar Companies Registry. FURTHER RESOLVED that [Director Name] be and is hereby appointed as first director and [Secretary Name] as company secretary, each to serve until the first annual general meeting, and that said officers be authorized to open corporate bank accounts, engage professional advisers, and execute all documents required to commence operations.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Gibraltar Companies Registry (online name search / physical counter)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a corporate name search on the Registry's online database to confirm the proposed name is not identical or confusingly similar to an existing registered company. Submit Form N1 (Name Reservation) with the preferred name and any acceptable variations; ensure the name ends with 'Limited' or 'Ltd' unless an exempt status or special licensing requirement permits otherwise.
required_dossiers: Power of attorney if submittal by agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused on grounds of similarity or prohibited expression, file a new and distinguishable name reservation within five business days using the same Form N1 procedure.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting and Execution of Constitutional Documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Subscriber / notary public / Gibraltar legal practitioner
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the Memorandum and Articles of Association in English, setting out the company's name, registered office clause, share capital, objects, director powers, and meeting provisions. The subscriber must sign the documents in the presence of a witness, and the signatures must be notarized or certified by a qualified legal practitioner for onward submission to the Registrar.
required_dossiers: Consent to act as first director and secretary
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registry queries any clause or the notarial attestation, file a revised conformed version through the authorized legal agent together with an explanatory letter within 10 business days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Gibraltar Companies Registry (online portal or counter)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit Form INC-G, the signed Memorandum and Articles of Association, and the Statement of Compliance to the Companies Registry. Pay the official filing fee (USD 90 or GBP equivalent) by credit transfer or card. Retain the date-stamped receipt as proof of valid submission.
required_dossiers: Memorandum and Articles of Association (signed and witnessed)
Registered office consent from the Gibraltar-licensed service provider
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is rejected for incompleteness, utilize the Registry's formal resubmission process within 14 calendar days; correct all defects and pay any applicable re-filing fee, or request an extension in writing before the 14-day period lapses.

step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon satisfactory review, the Registrar issues the Certificate of Incorporation assigning a unique company registration number. Electronic and hard-copy certified copies may be obtained; apostille certification is available for use in foreign jurisdictions.
required_dossiers: Copy of the filed incorporation set
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the certificate is delayed beyond the statutory SLA, submit a written expedite request to the Registrar stating the intended business opening date; if necessary, engage a Gibraltar lawyer to make a direct follow-up with the Registry.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: First directors / company secretary / registered agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the statutory register of members, register of directors and secretaries, register of charges, and minute books. Convene a written resolution of the first board to adopt the pro-forma resolutions, open a corporate bank account, and file any necessary notice of registered office (Form ROR) with the Registrar.
required_dossiers: Consent to act as director and secretary
First board meeting minutes or written resolution
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If any governance filing is rejected, submit the corrected version with an amendment cover letter; late statutory filings may attract a penalty, so a late filing justification memorandum should accompany the corrected form.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registered Agent Confirmation and Exempt Status Declaration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Gibraltar Companies Registry and HM Government of Gibraltar (Income Tax Office)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Confirm the formal appointment of a Gibraltar-licensed registered agent and file the corresponding appointment form with the Registry. If the company intends to rely on non-resident ownership/control for tax-neutral treatment, submit an exempt company declaration or standard 0% tax election to the Gibraltar Income Tax Office within 30 days of incorporation or as instructed by professional advisers.
required_dossiers: Exempt company declaration (Form EX-1) or tax election cover letter
Board resolution approving tax status election
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the exempt status filing is queried, respond to the Income Tax Office with a written explanation and a legal opinion from a Gibraltar counsel; the filing may be re-submitted within 21 days of the query notification.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable — digital stock photography and generative visual asset marketplace is a non-industrial activity under ISIC 7420; no manufacturing or physical production unit is established.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not applicable — no operating license required for commercial stock photo / AI visual asset distribution under Gibraltar laws.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Department of Environment, HM Government of Gibraltar
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt — activity has no physical premises, no manufacturing processes, and no controlled effluent; therefore no full EIA report or environmental registration is mandated.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not applicable — no wastewater, VOC, or waste-handling thresholds apply. To the extent data centres are used by cloud providers, those providers must comply with applicable EU/UK-equivalent environmental standards and the Carbon Reduction Commitment framework.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: No fire safety or structural load inspection is required for a purely digital service. Should a physical registered office or light office space be leased, the landlord must provide an up-to-date fire safety certificate and electrical installation condition report, and the company must complete a low-risk workplace risk assessment for general office occupation.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: HM Government of Gibraltar – Income Tax Office for direct taxation; HM Customs Gibraltar for indirect and customs matters; Gibraltar Companies Registry for corporate registration of overseas and external companies.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A Bermuda Exempted Company establishing a branch or place of business in Gibraltar must file an overseas company application with the Gibraltar Registrar of Companies within one month. The company must then apply to the Income Tax Office on Form 1 (Application for a Tax Reference Number), submitting constitutional documents, proof of registered office or agent in Gibraltar, details of directors and shareholders, and evidence of central management and control location. The Income Tax Office issues a Gibraltar Tax Reference Number (TRN) and determines resident or non-resident status. Non-resident companies deriving Gibraltar-source assessable income must register; entities with no PE and no Gibraltar-source income are not statutorily required to register, though a voluntary registration obtains a non-residence determination.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation / Tax_Exempt_Zone: The Bermuda Exempted Company is a separate corporate taxpayer in Bermuda, exempt from Bermuda income and capital gains tax by virtue of exempted status. In Gibraltar it remains an entity-level taxpayer under the Gibraltar Income Tax Act 2010. If centrally managed and controlled from Gibraltar, it is resident and assessable at the 10% corporate rate on worldwide income; otherwise it is non-resident and assessable only on Gibraltar-source income. The entity is not pass-through eligible.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Gibraltar has no check-the-box election. The company may elect to evidence non-residence by keeping central management and control outside Gibraltar. For US federal tax purposes, the entity may file Form 8832 to check-the-box as a disregarded entity or corporation; hybrid mismatch rules under Gibraltar's Income Tax (Companies) Act and OECD BEPS reports limit mismatches. A Bermuda-issued tax assurance certificate under the Exempted Undertakings Tax Protection Act 1966 can guarantee no Bermuda tax on profit, income, or capital until 2035, but it does not affect Gibraltar taxation.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: No VAT/GST in Gibraltar; indirect system consists of Customs Import Duty, Excise Duty, and Consumption Tax on selected goods. Digital stock-photo and AI-generated visual asset supplies are not subject to Gibraltar VAT/GST.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: N/A – Gibraltar does not operate a VAT-registration threshold. Gibraltar has no VAT registration for digital services. However, distance sales of digital services to EU Member State consumers may create OSS/VAT registration obligations outside Gibraltar once annual cross-border turnover exceeds EUR 10,000 in another Member State.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Gibraltar imposes no e-invoicing, real-time fiscal clearance, or digital stamping mandate. Standard commercial invoices with full taxpayer identification suffices. If the entity triggers VAT registration in an EU destination jurisdiction, that jurisdiction's e-invoicing or clearance rules (e.g., Italian SDI, French Factur-X/PPF, German XRechnung) will apply to those supplies only.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rated export treatment is not applicable because Gibraltar does not levy VAT. Digital deliveries of commercial stock photographs and AI-generated visual assets are outside the VAT zero-rating framework. For income tax substantiation, the company may claim that digital royalties and license fees are foreign-source if the purchaser is non-Gibraltarian, utilization occurs outside Gibraltar, and the contract is concluded and performed outside Gibraltar. Physical export of photographic media, if any, is not subject to export duty and requires standard customs documentation only where required by destination-country rules.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Gibraltar Customs Export Declaration (SAD/C88) – required only for physical goods, not digital deliveries
Bill of Lading or Airway Bill – for physical photographic media shipments
Commercial invoice and digital license agreement or media subscription contract
Inward Remittance Certificate or bank/PSP settlement statements evidencing FX repatriation
Digital delivery evidence such as server access logs, download URLs, license keys, and public-key verification records
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Gibraltar has no VAT fraud or zero-rating clawback because there is no VAT regime. Customs export misdeclarations for physical consignments are penalized under the Customs Ordinance 1992: for each offence up to £5,000, plus three times the value of duty evaded and forfeiture of goods. False claims of non-residence or foreign-source income expose the company to retrospective reassessment for up to six years (twenty years where fraud is established), interest at 8% per annum, and a 35% surcharge on any understated income tax under the Income Tax (Self-Assessment) (Amendment) Regulations. Artificial arrangements designed to shift stock-photo licensing income to the Bermuda exempted company may be counteracted under Gibraltar's General Anti-Abuse Rule with restated taxable profits and corresponding sanctions.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: HM Government of Gibraltar / Gibraltar Financial Services Commission (GFSC) — Gibraltar does not maintain an indigenous central bank; monetary supervision is undertaken by the GFSC while the Gibraltar pound (GIP) is statutory pegged at a 1:1 parity with British pound sterling and therefore operates under the monetary anchor of the Bank of England.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Gibraltar applies a full liberalisation regime for both current and capital account transactions. The Gibraltar pound is fully convertible at parity with GBP; profit remittance, dividend distributions, and capital returns are permitted without exchange-control authorisation or quantitative limits. The only applicable frictions are the standard AML/KYC documentation package, CRS/FATCA reporting, and the completion of a transparent ultimate beneficial ownership structure before a bank permits outbound remittances. For the targeted ISIC 7420 stock-photography and AI-generated visual-assets platform there are no sector-specific convertibility hurdles, no withholding surcharge on licensing revenue, and no restriction on retaining proceeds in GBP, EUR, USD, or other freely convertible currencies.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: There are no statutory export-proceeds surrender requirements, mandatory conversion ratios, or repatriation deadlines under Gibraltar law. All export and marketplace revenues may be retained or freely converted in GIP, GBP, USD, EUR, or any suitable settlement currency; no obligation exists to convert foreign receivables into GIP or to surrender receivables to a central authority.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational multi-currency current account (GBP/EUR/USD) for marketplace collections, disbursements, and daily cash management
Capital Escrow Account and corporate treasury facility
Corporate current account with private-banking overlay for FX and liquidity management
Segregated client-money operating account for higher-touch relationship banking

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: High viability for marketplace collections and disbursement operations, but only as an auxiliary clearing layer. Licensed UK EMIs such as Wise Business, Revolut Business, Payer, and the Stripe Treasury / PayPal treasury rails are suitable for merchant settlement in GBP/EUR/USD and low-value contributor payouts. Legal constraints are: (i) an offshore EMI is not a full-service bank and will not act as a capital escrow provider or long-term treasury depository; (ii) a physical branch or substantive EMI presence in Gibraltar would require a GFSC Electronic Money Licence under the Financial Services Act 2019; and (iii) EMIs may block or curtail high-frequency IP-licence and AI-generated content settlement unless the platform supplies separate sales-provenance data, volume forecasting, and an AML-compliant merchant-of-record structure.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Remote account opening is accepted for low-risk online stock-media and AI-asset platforms by most Gibraltar tier-1 banks and almost all UK EMIs, subject to a live video KYC interview, 100-point corporate identification, and source-of-funds evidence. For the higher-touch private banks, physical attendance by one director or the ultimate beneficial owner, or equivalent attendance before a notary public/embassy official with apostille-legalised documents, is normally required as enhanced due diligence. Because the legal vehicle is a Bermuda Exempted Company, the bank will additionally require a Bermuda Certificate of Good Standing, Certificate of Incorporation, Register of Directors and Members, notarised board resolution, and a Gibraltar-licensed legal opinion confirming the entity is not a passive or offshore shell.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Bermuda exempted-company opacity and unverified ultimate beneficial ownership
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide: (i) a transparent beneficial ownership register mapping every natural-person owner above the effective 25% threshold; (ii) registered-agent validation letter; (iii) Bermuda corporate records with certificate of incumbency and certificate of good standing; (iv) Gibraltar/UK registered-office and economic substance filing evidence; (v) notarised board resolution appointing all authorised signatories; and (vi) a Gibraltar-licensed counsel legal opinion confirming the corporate purpose and disclaiming passive investment-vehicle status.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: AI-generated visual assets and high-volume digital IP royalty-style revenue raising concern about market abuse, sanctions, and IP provenance
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Deliver an end-to-end provenance and monetisation pack: audited sales dashboard for the stock-photo marketplace; merchant-of-record agreements with Stripe and PayPal; end-user licence terms; contributor payout schedules; AI model-training provenance records; machine-generated content moderation policy; sanctions and adverse-media screening results; and a compliance certificate showing that all imagery is free of unlawful, infringing, or prohibited-content files.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border third-party processor collections through Stripe/PayPal creating high-volume, non-face-to-face, small-ticket transaction profile
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Compile an AML/CTF programme containing: internal KYC and onboarding procedures; transaction monitoring and velocity rules; automated sanctions screening protocols; SOC 2 or ISO 27001 attestation of the platform infrastructure; third-party payment processor due-diligence files and signed financial-services agreements; a sample of contributor payout invoices with matching banking remittance data; and a complete trust sheet proving that funds flows correspond to genuine licensing and subscription activity, thereby responding to layering and structuring red flags.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound share capital and working capital injections into the Gibraltar corporate bank account must be sent via SWIFT MT103 using the remitter's own bank account, with the beneficiary Gibraltar account referenced in field 59, the correspondent bank in field 57C when applicable, and the remitter in field 50K. The stated purpose code should be 'Capital contribution / subscription for shares' and the ISO 20022 remittance information should include the reference GB__GI__BM_EXEMPTED_CO__ISIC_7420_01_COMMERCIAL_STOCK_PHOTO_AI plus the underlying board resolution number. No exchange-control approval is required, but the receiving bank will request: notarised board resolutions, shareholder subscription or loan agreements, audited financial statements where relevant, bank statements of the remitter, CRS/FATCA self-certification, and confirmation that the injection is not derived from third-party uncontrolled funds. Verification time for a low-risk profile is typically 3-7 business days, with mandatory GFSC AML reporting triggered for transactions above the standard reporting threshold.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound contributor royalties, licensing residuals, production payments, and trade disbursements can be cleared through the following rails: (i) SWIFT MT103 for international non-UK/EU transactions with the purpose stated as 'licensing royalty' or 'invoice settlement'; (ii) UK Faster Payments and CHAPS for GBP denominated contributor and supplier payments routed through London clearing; (iii) SEPA EUR rails where the Gibraltar bank participates in euro clearing via its UK/EU correspondent relationship; and (iv) commercial irrevocable letters of credit only for high-value buy-out deals in which the platform is the intermediary purchaser and needs documentary payment security. Each outbound payment must pass OFAC, HM Treasury, and EU/UN sanctions screening and be traceable to verified inbound proceeds to prevent layering and compliance breach.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Plain-vanilla spot FX contracts for same-day settlement of GBP/EUR/USD balances
Outright GBP/EUR and GBP/USD forward contracts up to 24 months entered into with an authorised Gibraltar bank or licensed UK counterparty
Cross-currency swaps on EUR/USD and GBP/EUR axes for genuine treasury hedging of the licensing and subscription cash flows

Deliverable GIP/GBP parity forwards for local operating expense management; non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) are generally unavailable or quoted only as synthetic GBP products because GIP is pegged at par to GBP

FX options are permitted only where the platform holds the necessary GFSC investment-business or ancillary-services licence; speculative margined or unhedged retail FX trading on the platform account is expressly disallowed.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Bermuda Exempted Company Annual Return (Form AR) with Certificate of Compliance
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registrar of Companies, Government of Bermuda
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 days after the anniversary date of incorporation, annually
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing incurs a BMD 500 penalty for the first default window with escalating cumulative penalties for continued failure; default in excess of six months enables the Registrar to strike the company off and vest its assets in the Crown.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Bermuda Economic Substance Act Annual Declaration (ESD Filing via BESR Online)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Bermuda Economic Substance Registry, Ministry of Finance
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within six months after the end of the financial year (by 30 June for a 31 December year-end)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file attracts penalties up to BMD 10,000 per annum and up to BMD 100,000 for false declarations; persistent breach may trigger strike-off and director disqualification.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Gibraltar Foreign Company Annual Return (Part 22, Companies Act 2014)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Gibraltar Registrar of Companies (Companies House, GFSC)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 42 days after the anniversary of the company's registration in Gibraltar, annually
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing is subject to Registrar penalties up to GIP 1,000; non-filing for six months or more exposes the foreign company to strike-off from the Gibraltar Register and personal fines for directors.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Gibraltar Annual Accounts Delivery (abridged small-company accounts or full accounts as applicable)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within nine months after the Gibraltar accounting reference date (commonly 31 December); first filing period is aligned to the company's ARD election
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Civil late-filing penalties escalate up to GIP 1,000; continued default triggers compulsory strike-off and disqualification of the Gibraltar authorized representative.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Bermuda: mandatory independent audit applies only to 'auditable entities' (stock-exchange-listed companies, regulated financial licensees such as banks, insurers, fund administrators and fiduciary licensees, and their holding entities); an exempted company may dispense with audit by shareholder resolution. Gibraltar: audit is compulsory only where the registered foreign company fails the small-company test (two of three: turnover exceeding GIP 10.2M; balance sheet exceeding GIP 5.1M; average employees exceeding 50); a stock-photo AI platform below these limits remains audit-exempt.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Bermuda: IFRS (or US GAAP for SEC-registrants and regulated entities); Bermuda-incorporated exempted companies are not required to file annual accounts publicly. Gibraltar: IFRS as endorsed or Gibraltar GAAP (FRS 102 basis) for small entities; small companies may deliver abridged accounts with the annual return.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Bermuda: maintain a Register of Beneficial Owners (RBE) at the registered office; file non-resident beneficial ownership particulars with the Registrar and re-verify UBO data annually at the time of the annual return; any shareholding transfer triggers an RBE update within 30 days. Gibraltar: as a Part 22 foreign company, maintain a Gibraltar UBO register; file a UBO confirmation snapshot with the Registrar within 14 days of any shareholding transfer and complete an annual validation with the annual return cycle.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members, Register of Directors, Minute Book

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: US$2,500–US$4,500 per annum (US$1,500–US$2,500 for Bermuda registered office and resident secretary; US$1,000–US$2,000 for Gibraltar registered office and licensed agent)
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: US$5,000–US$10,000 per annum when a certified statutory audit is triggered; nil for audit-exempt small entities
